index.subtitle: Pure Mathematician and track and field sprinter
paragraphs: Hello! I'm Kasieobi Udumaga, a high school student from British Columbia, Canada with a strong interest in pure mathematics.

My primary interests include algebra, algebraic number theory, commutative algebra, and arithmetic geometry. This website documents my learning, research projects, expository writing, and mathematical notes.

Outside of mathematics, I am a sprinter and love track and field. I am a 12 time provincial champion in the 100m and 200m. I also hold the tied electronically timed provincial record in the U15 100m dash.

Hi! I'm Kasieobi Udumaga, a high school student who's been captivated by mathematics since I was in first grade. There's something incredibly satisfying about unraveling a tricky proof or discovering an unexpected connection between different areas of math.

My dream is to contribute to mathematical research and share what I learn through writing and teaching. I believe mathematics is not just about solving problems—it's about exploring beautiful ideas and making them accessible to others.
Feel free to reach out if you'd like to chat about math, discuss a problem, or just connect with another math enthusiast!
More about my journey will be added here soon!

welcome.heading: Get in Touch
paragraphs: I love connecting with fellow math enthusiasts—whether you want to discuss a tricky problem, share feedback, or just chat about the beauty of mathematics. Don't be shy!
I do my best to respond to everyone, though it might take a few days during busy periods (especially during exam season 😅).

notes.intro: Welcome to my collection of mathematical notes. This page is a growing library of notes that I have written while learning and exploring different areas of mathematics, ranging from olympiad topics to undergraduate and graduate subjects. Mathematics is best understood through examples, proofs, problem solving, and revisiting ideas over time, and these notes reflect that process. Most of these notes are living documents that will continue to be refined and expanded as I learn more. I hope they are useful to students, problem solvers, and anyone with an interest in mathematics, and that they encourage others to explore the beauty, creativity, and depth of the subject.

expository.subtitle: Mathematical exposition, problem analysis, and experimental mathematics.
paragraphs: Expository writing is one of the most important forms of mathematical communication. Its purpose is not to present new research, but rather to explain existing mathematics in a clear, logical, and accessible way. A well-written exposition bridges the gap between technical rigor and intuition, helping readers understand not only what is true, but also why it is true and how different ideas are connected. This page is my personal collection of expository articles spanning several areas of mathematics. It is organized into sections covering olympiad mathematics, undergraduate topics, and graduate-level subjects, each containing notes, expository essays, problem discussions, and surveys of interesting mathematical ideas. Some articles are intended to introduce foundational concepts, while others provide detailed solutions, commentary, historical context, or connections to more advanced mathematics.
